exposure: All-trans retinoic acid (40, 45, 50 mg/kg) exposure on gestational day 11
Olive oil (control) exposure on gestational day 11
cohort: Newborn rat pups exposed to varying doses of all-trans retinoic acid or olive oil during fetal development on gestational day 11.
finding: High doses of retinoic acid exposure during fetal development significantly reduced pup weight, increased mortality, and impaired bladder function, while mostly not significantly affecting general sensorimotor function except for increased facial wiping at a 40 mg/kg dose.
birth_weight: Measured as an outcome (pups exposed to 45 and 50 mg/kg RA weighed significantly less)
